Build note — React art prototype starter pieces (all tabs left open)

1) IDE — JetBrains WebStorm (tab 1, jetbrains.com/webstorm)
- "The JavaScript and TypeScript IDE" — the sensible default JetBrains IDE for web code. Free for non-commercial use (fits a prototype); ready out of the box with JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, React, Angular, Vue, Node.js, Git, debugger, terminal, Prettier/linters.

2) Cartoon mouse PNG, verifiably transparent (tab 2)
- Source: Wikimedia Commons — File:Angrymice.png (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Angrymice.png)
- Verified on the file page: original file 639 × 678 px, 209 KB, image/png; categorized "Animals on transparent background", "Mouse cartoons", "Cartoon characters", "Anthropomorphic mice". License CC-BY-SA 3.0 (credit "Nugetss", Wikimedia Commons) — attribution required if you ship it.
- Backup option (tab 8): favpng.com/free-png/cartoon-mouse.html — 5,193 free cartoon-mouse transparent PNGs.

3) Stretchy (Taffy Tails) comparison (tab 3, taffy-tails.fandom.com/wiki/Stretchy)
- Stretchy is one of the main four candy monsters of Taffy Tails (Roblox), appearing on round 1 — an animated Taffy. He roams the candy factory, only sees in front of him, and runs down players he spots. Style cues: stretchy/elastic candy body, head "always flapping around", secondary mascot alongside Gummy, Sour, Fluffy.
- Note: it's a character from a commercial Roblox game — fine as a style reference, but avoid using the actual in-game art/assets in your promo.

4) SVG → React component via react-svgr (tab 6, github.com/gregberge/svgr)
- Verified from the official README:
  npx @svgr/cli --icon --replace-attr-values "#063855=currentColor" -- icon.svg
- Its example output (verbatim from the README):
  import * as React from 'react'
  const SvgComponent = (props) => (
    <svg width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 48 1" {...props}>
      <path d="M0 0h48v1H0z" fill="currentColor" fillRule="evenodd" />
    </svg>
  )
  export default SvgComponent
- For your mouse, a simple source SVG like this:
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64" width="64" height="64">
    <circle cx="20" cy="18" r="10" fill="#f5a623"/>
    <circle cx="44" cy="18" r="10" fill="#f5a623"/>
    <ellipse cx="32" cy="38" rx="18" ry="20" fill="#f5a623"/>
    <circle cx="26" cy="34" r="2.5" fill="#222"/>
    <circle cx="38" cy="34" r="2.5" fill="#222"/>
    <circle cx="32" cy="42" r="3" fill="#e05252"/>
  </svg>
  run through `npx @svgr/cli --icon mouse.svg` becomes (illustrative output of the standard SVGR transform — camelCased attrs, props spread, default export):
  import * as React from 'react'
  const SvgComponent = (props) => (
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64" width="1em" height="1em" {...props}>
      <circle cx="20" cy="18" r="10" fill="#f5a623" />
      <circle cx="44" cy="18" r="10" fill="#f5a623" />
      <ellipse cx="32" cy="38" rx="18" ry="20" fill="#f5a623" />
      <circle cx="26" cy="34" r="2.5" fill="#222" />
      <circle cx="38" cy="34" r="2.5" fill="#222" />
      <circle cx="32" cy="42" r="3" fill="#e05252" />
    </svg>
  )
  export default SvgComponent

5) CapCut (tabs 4, 5, 7)
- Web project → desktop app: Yes. Per CapCut's official help (tab 7, capcut.com/help/access-cloud-space-capcut-pc): make sure CapCut Desktop is current (Settings → Version → "Check for updates"), then in the desktop app click "Spaces" on the left — your Cloud space and shared team spaces appear there; you must be signed into the same account (email/Google/TikTok), since Cloud content is tied to the specific account. capcutguide.com (tab 4) corroborates: move the editable project via Spaces (upload/sync the project, open it on the destination, then verify timeline, media, fonts, export) — don't rely on copying a raw draft folder as a transfer.
- Background color behind an imported photo: Per CapCut's own guide (tab 5, capcut.com/resource/change-image-background-color): 1) open CapCut and upload the image; 2) run auto background removal on the image; 3) open the "Background" menu and choose "Background color" — pick from the color palette (you can fine-tune the color); 4) one-click apply; 5) export/download in your chosen format/size. (For a desktop video timeline, the equivalent is: photo on the top track, solid-color background layer on the track below.)

Open tabs kept for you: 1) WebStorm, 2) Angrymice.png file page (Commons), 3) Stretchy wiki, 4) CapCut project transfer guide, 5) CapCut background-color guide, 6) react-svgr GitHub README, 7) CapCut Cloud Space PC help, 8) FavPNG cartoon mouse collection.
